To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the braking process underlying the voluntary movements of the forearm consists of a first phase of braking due to viscoelastic forces, which is followed by a phase during which the agonist and antagonist muscle activities are organized in well defined bursts of electromyographic activity.
“the braking process of a movement can be divided into two stages, the first one being a viscoelastic process and the second a process involving the activation of antagonist muscles”.
the braking of voluntary forearm movements is a two-phase process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the motor control mechanisms underlying the braking process of the movement, and with the role of the passive visco-elastic properties of the muscles in the braking process.
the identification of the basic unit of movement in the motor system of man.
the identification of the basic units of movement and the way in which they are organized into complex patterns of muscle activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the braking process is organized in two phases.
, in the case of a voluntary movement of the forearm, the braking process is the result of the interaction of the passive visco-elastic forces and the motor output.

the unit of movement is organized to reduce the number of possible patterns to a limited number of basic patterns, which can be combined in various ways to generate the large number of voluntary movements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the unit of movement is a basic pattern of activation of muscles, organized in such a way that the agonist and antagonist muscle forces are balanced during the movement, and the movement is stopped by the passive visco-elastic tension developed by these muscles.
the unit of movement is organized to reduce the number of possible patterns for the activation of the muscles of a joint.
a single unit of movement is defined by the agonist and antagonist EMG bursts and that the duration of the agonist burst is the main determinant of the peak velocity of the movement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the unit of movement is organized around a single peak of velocity.
the motor system has developed a strategy for controlling the movement that allows it to be executed with the same pattern of muscle activity, irrespective of the inertial load.

the unit of movement is a pattern of activation of antagonist and agonist muscles which is characterized by the duration of the agonist burst, by the onset of the antagonist burst, and by the relative timing of these two burst.
